Accordion.name: Accordion
Accordion.description: Coordinated disclosure group: single or multiple open sections, animated reveal, keyboard-operable triggers.
Accordion.dense: Disclosure group: items {id,title,content}; type single|multiple; variant contained|enclosed|divided; controlled openIds or defaultOpenId(s); animated grid-rows reveal; aria per region
forbiddenUse: put primary navigation inside an accordion. AT users land on
nest accordions more than one level deep. Two-level
ship long, scrollable panels. If the content scrolls inside

usage.description: Accordion coordinates a set of disclosure sections. In the default `type="single"` at most one stays open (opening another closes the previous); `type="multiple"` lets any number stay open for side-by-side reading. Pass `items` ({id, title, content}); drive it uncontrolled with `defaultOpenId`/`defaultOpenIds` or controlled with `openIds` + `onOpenChange`. `variant` switches between a bordered card group (contained) and flush hairlines (divided). For a single independent "show more" use ExpandableSection; if most readers need all the content, use plain headings instead of hiding it.

bestPractices.description: Use it for scannable reference content (FAQs, specs) where one section at a time is the point.
Keep titles short questions or labels; the trigger is a button, not a heading replacement.
Set defaultOpenId to the question most visitors came for.
Keep ids stable — they key the open state and the trigger/region ARIA pairing.
Do not hide task-critical content in an accordion; required steps must be visible by default.
Use type="multiple" when users compare sections side by side (feature lists, pricing tiers); keep the default type="single" for FAQs and settings where one at a time is the point.
Do not put a single short paragraph behind a section — the click costs more than it saves; show the text directly.

examples.description: The canonical FAQ: one answer open at a time, opening the next closes the last, clicking the open item closes it.
defaultOpenId lands visitors on the entry most of them came for, with the rest one keypress away.
type=\"multiple\" keeps any number of sections open at once — use it when readers compare content across sections, like feature lists or pricing tiers.
Pass openIds + onOpenChange to drive the accordion from parent state — when open sections should sync with a URL param, form, or external control.
variant=\"enclosed\" wraps the group in a single rounded border with no dividers between rows — a seamless card. Row separation comes from spacing and the open/closed state.
variant=\"divided\" removes the container border for flush hairline separators — lighter weight for inline disclosure in sidebars or detail panels.
Mark an item disabled to show it in the set while its trigger is inert — for sections that are not yet available.
Triggers are real buttons: Tab reaches them, Enter or Space toggles, aria-expanded and aria-controls wire each trigger to its region — asserted by the play function.

AlertBanner.name: AlertBanner
AlertBanner.description: Inline alert for info, warning, success, and error feedback.
AlertBanner.dense: persistent inline status banner; tone info|success|warning|error drives icon + live-region politeness; title/description/action slots; opt-in dismissible with localized control
forbiddenUse: pair AlertBanner with a blocking Modal for the same user outcome — pick one surface.
make error banners dismissible: letting the user hide a blocking problem strands them mid-flow.
stack more than one banner on the same page; two competing persistent messages cancel each other out.
animate the banner in on every render; it is persistent chrome, not a transition.

usage.description: AlertBanner is the persistent, page-level status surface: it encodes severity through both color and an announced icon, carries an optional title, rich description, and action slot, and stays put until the user reads (or dismisses) it. Errors interrupt assistive tech automatically (role=alert, assertive); every other tone is a polite status. It has no auto-dismiss by design — transient confirmations belong to Toast.

bestPractices.description: Pick tone by outcome severity; the error tone switches to role=alert with assertive announcement on its own — no ARIA wiring needed.
Pass both title and description for messages that read as a small document; description accepts nodes, so links and inline formatting are fine.
Put the follow-up in the action slot (a tertiary Button works best) instead of burying a link inside the prose.
Use dismissible with onDismiss for non-critical notices the user should acknowledge once; persist the dismissal in the consumer.
Do not use AlertBanner for transient feedback — it has no auto-dismiss because "sit here until acknowledged" is its job. Use Toast for post-action confirmations.
Do not make error banners dismissible; the user should not be able to hide the explanation of a blocked flow.
Do not stack multiple banners on one page; consolidate into the single most severe message.

AspectRatio.name: AspectRatio
AspectRatio.description: Layout primitive that locks its children to a fixed width/height ratio (1:1, 4:3, 16:9, …) so media-shaped containers reserve space before content loads.
AspectRatio.dense: Ratio box (1:1|4:3|16:9 default|21:9|3:2|2:3) with absolutely-filled child and overflow hidden; media inside should fill (object-cover) — reserves space, prevents CLS
forbiddenUse: Use this as a generic flex/grid item — pick a layout primitive instead.
Add padding or margin via className — children will overlap their own padding because the wrapper is `position: relative`.

usage.description: AspectRatio reserves a proportional box and absolutely fills it with its child, clipping overflow. Wrap media — images, video embeds, map iframes — and let the child fill (width/height 100%, object-fit cover). Because the box takes its height from the ratio, it also works as a CLS-free placeholder while media loads. 16:9 is the default; 1:1 suits avatars and thumbnails.

bestPractices.description: Make the child fill: width/height 100% and object-fit cover for images.
Use 16:9 for video, 1:1 for square thumbnails, 3:2 for editorial photography.
Wrap lazy media in it so the page reserves space up front (no layout shift on load).
Combine with Skeleton inside for a loading placeholder at the final footprint.
Do not put text layouts inside — overflow hidden clips anything the ratio cannot fit.
Do not nest ratio boxes; one box defines the frame, the child just fills it.

examples.description: The preset ratios: 16:9 for video, 1:1 for thumbnails, 3:2 for editorial photography. The child fills and clips.

Media fills the frame with width/height 100% and object-fit cover, so a source of any ratio crops to the frame instead of distorting. The same square (1:1) source is shown two ways in identical 16:9 frames — contain reveals the whole source (note the top/bottom bands), cover fills the frame and clips those bands away.
Because the height comes from the ratio, the frame reserves space before media loads — no layout shift; pair with Skeleton for the placeholder.

Avatar.name: Avatar
Avatar.description: Profile image, initials, link, or menu trigger.
Avatar.dense: Identity mark: image (srcSet/lazy) or initials from name; sm..xl sizes; optional link (clickable + destinationUrl) or dropdown menu (menuItems + menuLabel); variant forces image|initials
forbiddenUse: render two interactive children inside Avatar (link plus menu);
nest an Avatar inside a Button. Pick one — Avatar already owns

usage.description: Avatar renders a person or entity mark: the image when `imageUrl` resolves, otherwise initials derived from `name`. It scales through the size tokens and can act as a link (`clickable` + `destinationUrl`) or as a menu trigger (`menuItems` + `menuLabel`) with an in-place dropdown. Always pass `name` — it feeds both the initials fallback and the accessible naming.

bestPractices.description: Always provide name, even with an image — it is the initials fallback and the accessible name.
Provide srcSet/sizes for photographic avatars so dense grids do not ship desktop images to mobile.
Use menuLabel to say what the menu does ("Account menu"), not who the person is.
Keep loading lazy (default-friendly) in long lists; eager only above the fold.
Do not wrap Avatar in another link/button when clickable or menuItems already make it interactive — nested controls break AT.
Do not use variant="initials" to hide a broken image pipeline; fix the source, the fallback is for genuinely imageless users.

examples.description: Photographic avatar: imageUrl renders the image; still pass name in real use — it is the fallback and the accessible name.
No image, no problem: initials derive from name. This is the honest fallback, not a style choice for broken pipelines.

menuItems + menuLabel turn the avatar into an account-menu trigger. The dropdown is the shared Menu primitive (Radix): aligned rows, collision-aware placement, and full keyboard support. The label names the menu, not the person.

usage.description: AvatarGroup answers "who is on this?" at a glance: the first max Avatars overlap into a stack and the remainder collapses into a +N bubble that also announces itself to screen readers. Pass same-size Avatars and set the matching group size (sm=2rem, md=2.5rem, lg=3rem) so the bubble lines up.

bestPractices.description: Keep max between 3 and 5; past that the stack stops being scannable and the +N carries the message.
Match children Avatar sizes to the group size so the overflow bubble aligns with the faces.
Name the cluster with ariaLabel ("Project members") — the group role reads it before the names.
Order children by relevance; the first faces are the ones people see.
Do not mix Avatar sizes in one stack; the overlap rhythm breaks.
Do not use the +N bubble as a button; if the full roster matters, link to it separately.

Badge.name: Badge
Badge.description: Compact status label with an orthogonal variant (visual weight) and tone (semantic colour), a size, and an optional icon.
Badge.dense: compact status pill; variant (filled/outlined) x tone matrix, sm/md/lg, auto status icon per tone, removable filter-chip mode, optional role=status live counter
forbiddenUse: rely on colour alone to convey tone — pair it with the icon or include
nest a Button inside a Badge beyond the built-in removable affordance.

usage.description: Badge carries a short piece of meaning, a state, a count, or a tag, in a compact pill. Two orthogonal axes encode the look: variant for visual weight (primary filled, secondary outlined) and tone for semantic color. A matching status icon is auto-resolved for non-neutral tones, and removable turns the badge into a dismissible filter chip.

bestPractices.description: Use tone to encode state (success, warning, error, info) and keep the label to a word or two.
Use removable with onRemove for filter chips; the built-in dismiss button ships with a translated accessible name.
Use role=status only for live counters that update at runtime; aria-live=polite announces changes without moving focus.
Use variant=secondary (outlined) when a filled badge would compete with nearby primary actions.
Do not put role=status on a static badge; live-region churn is wasted when the content never changes.
Do not use Badge as an interactive action or toggle; use Button for actions and Switch or Checkbox for state.
Do not encode meaning with tone alone; the label must carry the meaning for color-blind users.

Filter-chip mode; the dismiss affordance is an internal Button with a translated accessible name.
Custom icon next to the label via the icon slot.

Breadcrumb.name: Breadcrumb
Breadcrumb.description: Navigation trail with current page indication.
Breadcrumb.dense: Location trail: nav[aria-label=Breadcrumb] > ol; items {label, href?} in root->current order; last (or href-less) item renders as plain current text, earlier ones as Link sm; '/' separators
forbiddenUse: include the home icon as a separate item. Use `label: 'Home'`
skip levels to make the trail shorter. If the user is at
render the breadcrumb above a hero — it gets lost. Place it

usage.description: Breadcrumb renders the page's location trail as a labelled nav landmark containing an ordered list. Pass `items` in root-to-current order; entries with `href` render as links except the last, which always renders as the current page in plain text. Middle entries without `href` render as text too, so levels without landing pages stay honest. Keep labels short — a breadcrumb is orientation, not prose.

bestPractices.description: Order items root -> current; the last item is the page the user is standing on.
Keep the default aria-label ("Breadcrumb") unless a page carries two different trails.
Point hrefs at real route segments so every linked level is actually navigable.
Omit href on middle levels that have no landing page; they render as plain text instead of dead links.
Do not start every trail with the site name; begin at the section root ("Home" at most).
Do not hand-author "…" items to fake a collapsed middle — collapsing is not supported; shorten labels or drop levels instead.

anatomy.description: nav element with aria-label (default "Breadcrumb") so AT lists it among page landmarks.

examples.description: The underline prop is forwarded straight to each Link, so the trail behaves exactly like a Link: `always` keeps the wavy underline on, `hover` reveals it on hover and keyboard focus, and `none` omits it. There is no separate breadcrumb underline — Link owns it entirely.

Set homeIcon to render the first item as a house icon instead of a text label. The item's label stays the icon's accessible name, so screen readers still announce it; the icon carries no wavy underline.

Pass maxItems to collapse a long trail deterministically (no measuring): the first maxItems − 2 leading items and the current item stay visible, and the middle levels move into an ellipsis menu (the shared Menu primitive). The current page is always shown. The ellipsis glyph flips to a chevron while the menu is open.

With no maxItems, the trail measures itself against its container and collapses only when it cannot fit, keeping as many leading items as possible plus the current page, and re-expands on resize. Shown in a narrow 340px container so the overflow collapses; widen it and the hidden levels return.
Items render in root-to-current order; the last one is always plain text with no self-link. Keep labels short — the trail is orientation, not headline copy.
Omit href on levels that have no page of their own — they render as text instead of dead links. Collapsed middles (\"…\") are not supported; shorten labels or drop levels instead.
The nav landmark defaults to aria-label=\"Breadcrumb\". Override it only when a page carries two different trails, so screen-reader users can tell the landmarks apart.

Write labels that name the action, like Save changes or Send message, never OK or Click here.

Use clickAction for async work so the button shows its loading state and dedupes clicks automatically; if you need a progress readout (e.g. percent complete), render it yourself in children, the component only owns the busy/disabled state.
Pair tone=error with a confirmation step for irreversible actions.
Use surface=onDark or onBrand when the button sits on a dark or brand background instead of overriding colors.
Do not place more than one primary button in the same view; it dilutes the hierarchy.
Do not use Button for pure navigation; if it only takes the user to another page, use Link (Button with href is for action-shaped navigation like Get started).
Do not encode meaning with tone alone; the label must carry the meaning for color-blind users.
Do not use Button for an on/off state; use Switch. For multi-select within a group, use Checkbox or CheckboxGroup.

Name the group with ariaLabel ("Text alignment", "View") so AT users get the context first.

Card.name: Card
Card.description: Quiet bordered surface for discrete, self-contained content; structure by composition.
Card.dense: Quiet bordered surface: variant default (hairline)|muted|transparent, padding none|sm|md|lg; title (xxs h3)/description/extra; link = ONE stretched anchor; loading = skeleton+status; compose the rest

usage.description: Card is the quiet surface for discrete, self-contained content — things that could be reordered, removed, or interacted with independently. The container owns background, hairline border, radius, and padding; `variant` only swaps the background (default with hairline, muted, transparent) and `padding` picks a step on the space scale. A thin content layer covers the common patterns: `title` (a real heading at xxs), `description`, and a right-aligned `extra` slot. Everything richer — dividers, footers, media, tabs — is composition with Divider, FlexBox, Stack, and friends. `link` turns the whole card into exactly one anchor with the focus ring on the frame.

bestPractices.description: Compose structure: Title/Text children, a Divider where the split carries meaning, a FlexBox row as the footer — the card is just the surface.
Keep padding consistent across sibling cards in a grid; pick one step per surface.
Set titleProps.level to keep the document outline honest — grids under a section heading typically use level 3.
Pass linkLabel on linked cards whose title is ambiguous out of context; "Read more" is the failure mode.
Use muted for de-emphasised siblings and transparent to group without visual weight — reach for spacing and headings before adding cards at all.
Do not nest interactive controls inside a link-mode card; use a plain card with a single Button instead.
Do not wrap page sections or whole forms in cards, and never nest cards in cards — that is Section/Stack territory.
Do not use the muted variant to encode status; status belongs to AlertBanner or Badge.
Put the destructive/special action in footerStart and the confirm/cancel buttons in footerEnd; footerEnd hugs the right even when footerStart is empty.
When you replace the title with custom headerStart content, keep a real heading inside it so the document outline stays honest.

Do not combine link mode with the action footer: a stretched anchor cannot wrap buttons, so Card drops the link and warns in dev when footerStart/footerEnd are set. Likewise keep interactive content (a menu) out of a linked card's header — Card cannot detect a ReactNode's interactivity there, so that case is the consumer's responsibility.

anatomy.name: Header row

anatomy.name: Footer row

Group related actions with MenuSeparator and reserve MenuSub for genuinely nested choices; a flat menu is faster to scan.

Do not re-implement positioning or keyboard handling around Menu; Radix already provides collision, roving focus, typeahead, and Escape.

usage.description: Modal is the blocking overlay for focused, dismissible tasks: confirmations, short forms, and status dialogs. bestPractices.description: Keep the Modal mounted and toggle isOpen; it stores the previously focused element on open and restores it on close.
Always pass title — it is the dialog's accessible name. Untitled dialogs fall back to a generic aria-label="Dialog".
Use description for the one-line summary screen readers announce on open (wired to aria-describedby), then put the rest in children.
Use severity for status dialogs: it derives the header icon and promotes error/warning to role=alertdialog for assertive announcement.
Give destructive or two-way choices an explicit footer (Cancel + primary action); reserve the default OK-only footer for acknowledgements.
Do not nest modals or open one from another — swap the content of the open modal in place instead.
Do not add aria-live near or on the dialog; the role already announces and you get a double reading.
Do not use a modal for long reading or deep multi-step forms — content that deserves scrolling deserves a page or section.
